options.metric: Annual pedestrian casualties, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed on Brooklyn crash records.
options.denominator: No denominator; annual count of reported pedestrian casualties.
options.reason: A combined casualty count captures the overall recorded pedestrian harm burden while including both injuries and deaths.
options.answer: This only partly answers whether pedestrian safety improved: the annual Brooklyn count of pedestrian injuries plus deaths in police-reported crashes was 3,671 in 2013, reached 1,798 in 2020, and was 2,874 in 2025; the partial 2026 year is excluded.
options.interpretation: This answers only the recorded-harm part of the safety question: the chart groups by calendar year and counts pedestrian injuries plus deaths recorded on Brooklyn police-reported motor-vehicle crash rows in complete years 2013–2025, with no exposure denominator. The count was 3,671 in 2013, reached a series low of 1,798 in 2020, and was 2,874 in 2025; this is a defensible measure of recorded casualty burden, but it does not establish risk per pedestrian trip or overall safety. The data check found zero missing borough, date, injury, or death fields among 483,501 Brooklyn records from 2013 onward, and borough matching trims and normalizes uppercase values. The chart excludes 9,700 records from partial 2026 (2.0% of the check population; coverage ends June 11) and retains the complete 2013–2025 years.

options.metric: Annual count of crashes with at least one recorded pedestrian injury or death (number_of_pedestrians_injured > 0 or number_of_pedestrians_killed > 0).
options.denominator: No denominator; annual count of qualifying crashes.
options.reason: A crash-based count shows the frequency of casualty crashes while counting each crash once even when multiple pedestrians are injured.
options.answer: This only partly answers whether pedestrian safety improved: Brooklyn police-reported crashes with at least one pedestrian injured or killed numbered 3,498 in 2013, reached 1,724 in 2020, and numbered 2,766 in 2025; the partial 2026 year is excluded.
options.interpretation: This answers the frequency of casualty crashes, not overall pedestrian risk: it counts each Brooklyn police-reported crash record once if either pedestrian injury or pedestrian death is greater than zero, grouped by complete calendar year 2013–2025, without an exposure denominator. The count was 3,498 in 2013, reached a series low of 1,724 in 2020, and was 2,766 in 2025; this is defensible for describing how often a pedestrian-casualty crash was recorded, but it does not establish risk per pedestrian trip. The data check found zero missing borough, date, or pedestrian injury/death fields among 483,501 Brooklyn records from 2013 onward; borough matching trims and normalizes uppercase values. The chart excludes the 9,700 partial-2026 records (2.0% of the check population; coverage ends June 11) and uses complete years 2013–2025.

options.metric: Annual pedestrian deaths, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_killed on Brooklyn crash records.
options.denominator: No denominator; annual count of recorded pedestrian deaths.
options.reason: A fatality-only series isolates the most severe recorded pedestrian outcome instead of combining deaths with nonfatal injuries.
options.answer: This only partly answers whether pedestrian safety improved: Brooklyn police-reported crashes recorded 30 pedestrian deaths in 2013, a series low of 17 in 2020, and 39 in 2025; the partial 2026 year is excluded.
options.interpretation: This answers only the fatal-harm part of the safety question: the chart groups by calendar year and sums recorded pedestrian deaths on Brooklyn police-reported motor-vehicle crash rows for complete years 2013–2025, with no exposure denominator. Recorded deaths numbered 30 in 2013, reached a series low of 17 in 2020, and numbered 39 in 2025; isolating fatalities is defensible because it focuses on the most severe outcome, but it does not measure overall safety or fatality risk per pedestrian trip. The data check found zero missing borough, date, or death fields among 483,501 Brooklyn records from 2013 onward, and borough matching trims and normalizes uppercase values. The chart excludes 9,700 records from partial 2026 (2.0% of the check population; coverage ends June 11) and retains complete years 2013–2025.
